agent.problem: The card cites only 1 John 1:1, but it also makes claims about the entire letter: that the writer never signs his name and never names his readers. Its statement that he writes directly to “you” also uses wording from later verses, not verse 1. The citation does not cover what the card uses.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: The word “this” has no antecedent within the question. Once the opening story card is gone, the baker is not told whether the question concerns the Word of life, what was from the beginning, or something else.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

agent.problem: Four of the stop's five choice cards are unsupported discovery questions. Cards 2, 6, 8 and 9 give the baker no earlier-card basis for reasoning out whether the account is secondhand, why the writer proclaims it, who the fellowship is with, or which additional purpose he gives. Discovery questions therefore dominate this stop rather than remaining a few exceptions.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the setup about fellowship, the sentence about not skimming the guest list, and the sentence about reading it twice.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the unseen wording of 1 John 1:5. Card 1 merely says that a big message is coming and gives no basis for reasoning out “light”; the passage title cannot serve as the missing setup.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

agent.problem: This story card runs to four punctuated sentence units: the setup about walking in darkness, the sentence about what the writer will say, “Well.” and “All mustache.” That exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: The first sentence retells Jesus's advocacy from 1 John 2:1, while the second tells the atoning sacrifice from 2:2. Citing only 2:2 leaves out the first verse the card uses.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: Marking this statement false establishes only that the sacrifice is not restricted to the letter's original readers. No card ever tells the baker that 1 John 2:2 explicitly includes “the sins of the whole world,” leaving the passage's final and important scope unstated.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: Multiple choice dominates both stops: four of five choice cards in stop 1 and six of nine in stop 2. There is only one fill-in-the-blank card in the entire walkthrough, so the question types are not naturally varied.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
